messages:
Lena (AE): BlueHarbor Capital signed the NDA and wants a 4-day POC. They insist on perimeter TLS inspection and want a single allowlist entry for outbound model traffic. Questions for the packet: can we support PrivateLink vs VPC peering with SNI-rewriting DPI? Also need a 2-line security blurb + short firewall snippet. @Diego @Maya @Avi

Diego (Solutions): Short answer: both patterns can work but have tradeoffs. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) keeps ingress local to customer subnets; our service side still egresses from Redwood IPs. If their DPI rewrites SNI or terminates TLS, certificate-based auth (including mTLS) can fail. Two recommended patterns:
- PrivateLink only: easiest to operate. Customer must avoid terminating TLS or implement cert re-issue so auth keeps working.
- Peering + connector: peer the VPCs or use a small connector VM in their VPC that talks to Redwood over outbound egress. This preserves original client IPs and lets the DPI see plaintext before it leaves their network.

Maya (NetOps): Pasteable firewall snippet (minimal):
```
# BlueHarbor POC - allowlist (example)
# Replace <REDFW_EGRESS> and <PRIVLINK_ENI_CIDR> with values we provide
ALLOW tcp from <app_subnets> to <PRIVLINK_ENI_CIDR> port 443
ALLOW tcp from <connector_subnets> to <REDFW_EGRESS> ports 443
ALLOW udp from <connector_subnets> to 8.8.8.8 port 53
# If peering: allow the peering CIDR blocks between customer VPC and connector VPC
ALLOW tcp from <customer_vpc_cidr> to <connector_vpc_cidr> ports 1024-65535
```

Maya (NetOps): Note on static IPs: for POC we can allocate a single static egress /32. For production HA we recommend a pair. If they need many allowlist entries, Dedicated is better (and cheaper per-IP at scale).

Avi (Security): 2-line blurb for their packet:
"Redwood will deploy an interface endpoint or lightweight connector into BlueHarbor-managed subnets for the POC. Outbound model requests will egress from Redwood-managed static IP(s) provided for the allowlist; if BlueHarbor performs TLS inspection that terminates TLS, Redwood recommends a connector deployment or a documented cert re-issue flow to preserve mutual authentication and audit logs."

Diego (Solutions): Quick pricing sketch to include in packet (estimates): static egress IP (POC) = $1,200/month (pro-rated); connector VM = $550/month + $1,000 one-time; peering/setup engineering fee = $2,000 (one-time). Dedicated capacity pricing on request.

Lena (AE): Action items: Diego to send the actual IP(s) + firm numbers by EOD Tue, Maya to attach a 1-page topology sketch and indicate minimal subnet sizes, Avi to drop the blurb into the security packet. deploy-bot: ticket POC-1602 created.

Diego (Solutions): Got it, will follow up with IPs and quote.

Maya (NetOps): Acknowledged, I'll share sketch Monday.

Avi (Security): Acknowledged, will add to questionnaire"
